title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Priya Shah
summary: Comprehensive playbook describing the Eval Harness onboarding flow, prompt set and benchmark standards, model onboarding checklist, quality guardrails, quantization profile guidance, and regression triage process for Redwood's Applied ML team.
body:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates the Applied ML team's standards and operational procedures for evaluation and model onboarding. It covers the Eval Harness onboarding steps, prompt set and benchmark guidelines, quality guardrails and monitoring, recommended quantization profiles, and a step-by-step regression triage and remediation process. The goal is to ensure consistent, reproducible evaluation across models and to reduce regression blast radius during rollouts.

Sections:
1) Eval Harness Onboarding

Intro:
- The Eval Harness is the canonical system for automated, reproducible model evaluation across prompt sets, metrics, and regression checks. Every new model and major model update must be registered and validated via the harness before production rollout.

Onboarding checklist (order matters):
1. Create model entry in Model Catalog: include model architecture, tokenizer, precision (fp16/int8), and expected KV-cache behavior. Owner: model-onboarding team.
2. Register model with Eval Harness: add model id, docker image or path, runner config, and baseline commit.
3. Provide canonical tokenization tests: include 10-20 edge-case sentences (truncation, special tokens, multilingual anchors).
4. Attach baseline prompt sets (see Prompt Sets section) and baseline metrics.
5. Run smoke eval: 3 short prompt sets (safety, hallucination, correctness) to validate basic responses within expected latency and memory.
6. Execute full eval run: compute full metric suite (BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, semantic similarity, factuality, safety scores, response-length distributions).
7. Review results with reviewers and sign off.
8. Publish model to internal staging registry and tag eval artifacts.

Required artifacts to attach to the harness entry (minimum):
- baseline-eval-report.json (automatically generated)
- prompt-sets-list.txt
- quantization-profile.md (if applying quantization)
- tokenization-tests.txt

2) Prompt Sets and Benchmark Guidelines

Purpose:
- Standardize prompt creation, labeling, and storage so that benchmarks are comparable and auditable. Prompt sets are categorized by capability (e.g., summarization, code generation), risk (safety-related), and workload characteristics (long context, multi-turn).

Prompt set standards:
- Metadata required: name, intent, domain, expected_output_type, languages, difficulty, rarity_flag.
- Each prompt entry must include: id, prompt_text, canonical_answer(s) when available, tags, and provenance (source/curation notes).
- Size targets: small test sets (50-200 prompts for quick smoke), medium (500-2k) for regular CI, large (5k+) for comprehensive periodic runs.

Benchmarking cadence:
- CI (per PR / model change): run small smoke sets for safety/correctness and latency.
- Nightly: run medium-sized sets for quality regressions and metric drift detection.
- Weekly/Monthly: run large sets including long-tail cases and cross-lingual coverage.

Example prompt metadata table (as plain text):
| field | example |
| name | summarization-news-english |
| intent | extractive summarization |
| expected_output_type | short_paragraph |
| languages | en |
| difficulty | medium |
| size | 1,000 |
| owner | applied-ml/team-templates |

3) Model Onboarding Guide (detailed)

Pre-acceptance requirements:
- Security scan of model artifacts (license, provenance). Owner: security-and-compliance.
- Checkpoint provenance: must include training dataset snapshot references and acceptable license flags.
- Privacy review if model trained on customer data.

Technical onboarding steps:
1. Artifact verification: ensure model weights, config.json, and tokenizer files are present.
2. Sanity runs: run the model on a standardized tokenization test and a 10-sample functional test set.
3. Performance profiling: capture latency P50/P95/P99, memory footprint, GPU utilization on the target serving instance (see Profiling Playbook).
4. Numerical stability checks: verify no NaN/Inf in logits over 100 randomized inputs.
5. KV cache stress test: run a 20k-token multi-turn session to validate cache correctness and memory behavior.
6. Compatibility tests: ensure the model runs across supported runtimes (xla/cuda/metal where applicable) if required.

Ownership and SLAs:
- Model owner must be assigned in the catalog.
- For hosted models, SLO: P95 latency < configured threshold (documented per-model) and no regressing quality metrics beyond threshold.

4) Quality Guardrails and Monitoring

Key guardrails:
- Safety filter integration: every model route must pass responses through a safety filter; set severity tiers (block, flag, soft-block).
- Factuality checks: automated factuality scoring for knowledge-intensive tasks; degrade to lower-capacity model or fall back to cached answers on low-confidence outputs.
- Output length and token budget enforcement.

Operational monitoring (metrics to emit):
- Per-route: latency P50/P95/P99, token throughput, error rate, safety flags per 1k responses.
- Per-model: metric drift (semantic similarity to baseline), hallucination rate, repetition rate, response entropy distribution.
- Alert thresholds: define alerting at 3-sigma above baseline for metric drift or when safety flag rate > 0.5% for 24h window.

Escalation flow for quality regressions:
1. Alert triggers on CI/nightly or production monitoring.
2. Triage by Applied ML on-call: validate metrics and reproduce with harness.
3. If regression confirmed, create incident and rollback policy check (see Regression Triage).

5) Quantization Profiles and Guidance

Purpose:
- Provide recommended quantization configurations (e.g., 8-bit, 4-bit) and tuning steps to reduce inference cost while minimizing quality loss.

Standard profiles (examples):
- q8_default: 8-bit symmetric quantization on linear layers; recommended for initial cost reduction.
- q4_mixed: 4-bit asymmetric + per-channel scaling on matmuls, keep attention softmax in fp16. For heavy throughput workloads.
- q4_opt_finetune: 4-bit with short post-quantization fine-tune on a 10k-example adapt set.

Profile metadata fields (plain list):
- name, precision, per-channel (yes/no), calibration_samples, expected_speedup, owner, notes.

Quantization checklist:
1. Baseline eval: run full benchmark on fp16.
2. Apply q8_default; run quick regression set (500 prompts).
3. If delta(metric) > tolerance, try q4_mixed with calibration.
4. Optionally run q4_opt_finetune and re-evaluate.
5. If quality still outside tolerance, fallback to fp16 for that route or use mixed-routing (route critical queries to fp16).

Recommended tolerances (team defaults):
- Semantic similarity drop <= 1.5% absolute for customer-facing routes.
- Safety metric must not regress (0 tolerance for safety-critical regressions).

Artifact naming convention: quantization-profile-<model>-<profile>-YYYYMMDD.md

6) Regression Triage Playbook (step-by-step)

Scope: any detected downstream quality regression in CI, nightly runs, or production telemetry.

Initial triage (first 30 minutes):
1. Confirm alert fidelity: validate alert, logs, and reproduce regression locally using the Eval Harness smoke set.
2. Identify change vectors: check recent model rollouts, quantization changes, prompt-set updates, routing changes, and infra changes.
3. Assign severity: Sev-1 if customer impact > 1% active routes or major SLA violations.

Containment steps (30-120 minutes):
1. Rollback or route to previous model variant / fp16 baseline if available.
2. Disable new quantization profile or routing policy.
3. Throttle traffic or apply sampling to isolate failure modes.

Root cause analysis (4-72 hours):
- Re-run full eval harness with side-by-side comparisons: baseline vs candidate vs quantized variant.
- Inspect failure clusters: by prompt category, language, length, or feature flags.
- Run differential token-level logits comparison for a sample set to find divergence points.

Remediation and verification:
1. If issue is model quality: revert rollout and either retrain or select a safer variant.
2. If issue is quantization: adjust profile, increase calibration samples, or apply per-layer exclusions.
3. If issue is prompt sets: update prompt or canonical answers and re-run CI.
4. Verification: must pass full nightly large benchmark and production canary with 24h observation before re-promote.

Post-incident actions:
- Postmortem documenting timeline, root cause, mitigations, and action items. Owner: incident lead.
- Update guardrail thresholds or alert rules if needed.
- Add new failing prompts to long-tail prompt repository and label for targeted improvements.

Appendices:
A) Useful CLI snippets:
- Run eval harness smoke: eval-harness run --model <model_id> --prompts smoke-set --out report.json
- Profile throughput: perf-tool profile --image <serving_image> --bs 8 --seq 1024 --out perf.json

B) Example metric JSON keys (flat list):
- semantic_similarity_score, factuality_score, safety_flag_rate, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, memory_bytes_peak

C) Contact and ownership matrix (names as points of contact):
- Eval Harness Owner: Priya Shah
- Model Onboarding Lead: Marco Ruiz
- Quantization SME: Liam Chen
- Applied ML On-call: applied-ml-oncall@redwood.example.com

D) Versioning and artifact retention:
- Eval artifacts retained for 180 days by default; long-term retention (2 years) for models tagged as "production-stable".

Document maintenance:
- Owner is responsible for annual review or after any major platform change (serving runtime, kernel changes, or routing policies).
- Suggested review schedule: quarterly reviewers, annual full audit.

References and related pages:
- See: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025.json
- See: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026.json

End of playbook.
